1.0: QUESTION: What is the most promising approach to solving the measurement problem in quantum mechanics, and why do physicists remain divided?
1.1: ASSERTS: The measurement problem has multiple competing approaches, each promising under different criteria (empirical testability, conceptual elegance, minimal departures from standard physics)
1.2: ASSERTS: The persistent division among physicists stems from these different value priorities, not lack of effort or time
2.0: DOCUMENT: Decoherence approach to measurement problem
2.1: ASSERTS: Decoherence explains absence of macroscopic superpositions through environmental interactions destroying quantum interference
2.2: ASSERTS: Decoherence is empirically confirmed and solves the preferred basis problem
2.3: REJECTS: Decoherence as complete solution - explains why world looks classical but not why particular outcomes occur
3.1: ASSERTS: Many-worlds takes Schrödinger equation as literally complete with all outcomes occurring in branching universes
3.2: ASSERTS: Many-worlds is mathematically elegant and requires no modifications to quantum mechanics
3.3: OPEN: Derivation of Born rule probabilities from deterministic splitting remains controversial
3.4: OPEN: Ontological status of branch weight unclear if all outcomes are equally real
4.1: ASSERTS: Objective collapse theories modify quantum mechanics to make wavefunction collapse physical at mass/complexity thresholds
4.2: ASSERTS: These theories are genuinely testable with active experimental searches for predicted deviations
4.3: REJECTS: Unitary evolution in objective collapse theories
4.4: OPEN: No convincing physical mechanism specified yet for collapse
5.1: ASSERTS: Pilot-wave theory has particles guided by quantum wavefunction, restoring determinism
5.2: ASSERTS: Reproduces all quantum predictions while being fully deterministic and visualizable
6.0: ASSERTS: Century-long stalemate exists because interpretations are not empirically distinguishable in most regimes
6.1: ASSERTS: Interpretations make radically different metaphysical commitments despite empirical equivalence
6.2: ASSERTS: Without experimental differentiation, physicists split along philosophical preferences
6.3: ASSERTS: Quantum mechanics keeps working perfectly regardless of interpretation, removing practical pressure to resolve the question
7.0: QUESTION: Is the square root of 2 an irrational number?
7.1: RESOLVED: The square root of 2 is an irrational number
